annotations.title: Measure subscriptions from bank outflows and received invoices

description:
Measure the workspace's subscriptions from its bank and credit card outflows: which suppliers it pays on a regular cadence, what each costs per month and per year, and how the spend moved month by month. It draws no card.

Call it when the user asks what they pay for on a regular basis, what their subscriptions cost, or how that spend moved. Then draw the two cards from its result, trend first:
  1. `well_render_category_trend` with one `category_trends` entry, passed as it is.
  2. `well_render_monthly_pivot` with the `pivots` entry of the same currency, passed as it is.
When the result holds more than one currency, draw one pair per currency. Never add two currencies together. When the result reads `success: true` and `partial: false`, `subscriptions` and `invoice_candidates` are empty, `other_workspaces_status` is not `unreadable`, `other_workspaces_skipped` is 0, and every `other_workspaces` entry reads `success: true`, `partial: false` and `rows_truncated: false` with its `subscriptions` and `invoice_candidates` empty too, no subscription was found: say so and draw nothing. When an `invoice_read.status` of a workspace read is not `read`, or `other_workspaces_empty_invoices_unread_count` is above 0, add that the received invoices of that workspace were not read. When the result reads `success: false` or `partial: true`, the subscriptions of this workspace are unknown: say so, never that no subscription was found. When an `other_workspaces` entry reads `success: false`, `partial: true` or `rows_truncated: true`, `other_workspaces_status` is `unreadable`, or `other_workspaces_skipped` is above 0, the subscriptions of that workspace are unknown: say so, never that no subscription was found. When a workspace read lists a subscription but `category_trends` and `pivots` are empty, the subscriptions were found and nothing falls in the drawn months: every subscription of this workspace was last debited before them, or only another workspace pays one. List the subscriptions, never say none was found, and draw nothing.

**The server applies every rule, and the result states each one in `rules`.** Quote the figures as returned: never recompute a cost, a total or a cadence, and never loosen a rule to list a supplier the user expects. A supplier in `not_recurring` missed the rule named in its `missed_rule`.

Every amount in the result is in the major units of its currency, never in cents: `1860` is 1,860.00 EUR, not 18.60 EUR.

The window is fixed: the last 24 complete calendar months in UTC and the running month are read, and the cards draw the last 12 complete months (the pivot draws the running month apart, marked as in progress). `window`, `current_month` and `display_months` say which months those were.

**A supplier row is a company or a bank label.** A row with a `company_id` is a company. A row whose `company_id` is null carries a `label_means_id` instead: a payee Well knows only by the label the bank prints, named by `name`, with no domain. List it like any other supplier, under its `name`. Never pass a `label_means_id` where a `company_id` is asked for: no contract, record or company lookup takes it.

What the result is:
  - `subscriptions`: the suppliers on a cadence (monthly, bimonthly, quarterly, yearly) whose category is software or a service paid on a schedule, largest cost per month first, at most 50; `subscription_count` is the full count, and a list that shows fewer says how many it shows. Each carries its cadence evidence, its amount pattern (fixed, changed, varying), the amount its cost per month starts from, the cost per month and per year, its latest month, `possibly_ended`, its category and `state` (possibly_ended, rising, falling, varying, stable): the one section it belongs to. Never list one supplier under two states.
  - `uncategorised_recurring`: suppliers on a cadence whose category says nothing about them (none, residual or suspense), at most 25; `uncategorised_recurring_count` is the full count and `uncategorised_recurring_monthly_total` their cost per month, one entry per currency, as decimal strings, over all of them and not only the listed ones. They are not counted as subscriptions and are in no total: give the count and the monthly total as leads (recurring payments Well cannot categorise yet, which may be subscriptions), and point the user to categorizing their counterparties. Never add the monthly total to `totals`.
  - `totals`: per currency, the subscription count, the total cost per month and per year, and the count and the cost per month of the subscriptions flagged as possibly ended (`possibly_ended_count`, `possibly_ended_cost_per_month`, already inside the count and the total).
  - `possible_duplicates`: subscription suppliers charged their own price more than once in a month. A lead to check, never a verdict, and never in a total. Taxes, meals, travel and a one-off transfer are never in it. A month whose `confirmed_distinct_pair` is true holds debits of one same amount, at most 7 days apart, one of them confirmed by a person as a separate payment: the bank took that charge twice, and `dispute_leads` holds it. Every other month is unsure.
  - `not_recurring`: suppliers paid in the window that are not subscriptions, at most 25, with the rule missed (one_month, too_few_months, multiple_debits_in_month, irregular_gaps, not_subscription_category). `not_subscription_category` is a supplier paid on a cadence whose category is work, fees or spend by use, such as an agency or a contractor: never call it a subscription.
  - `unattributed`: outflows whose payee resolves to no company and to no bank label, such as a person or a row with no payee. Real spend with no supplier to repeat, so never on a cadence.
  - `category_trends` and `pivots`: the render inputs, one per currency. A trend holds at most 6 lines, the smallest categories rolled into the last one.
  - `excluded`: what fell out, counted apart. `internal_transfers` are movements between the workspace's own accounts, card repayments among them. A charge on a credit card the workspace connected is measured like a bank debit, on the day of the charge and against its supplier, so its repayment is never counted a second time. `no_asset_movement` counts the outflows with no leg on an owned bank account or credit card: rows whose payer resolved to no account, a charge on a card that is not connected among them. Say so whenever the count is not zero: payments on rows linked to no connected account are NOT measured here. `payments_to_own_accounts` are payments to another owned account, such as a loan, `own_company` payments to the workspace's own company, `unreadable_rows` rows with no readable amount or currency. `category_keys` lists the categories never counted as subscriptions (transfers, treasury, loans, taxes, salaries, social charges), and `category_excluded` is how many bank outflows those categories removed. `internal_transfers` counts a transfer whatever its category. A `null` count was not measured, which is not zero.

**Received invoices.** Beside the bank, the tool reads the workspace's received supplier invoices, under `rules.invoice_source`. `invoice_candidates` lists the suppliers on a cadence from their invoices that no bank row lists: two invoices one cadence apart, or one invoice that states its period. Largest cost per month first, at most 50; `invoice_candidate_count` is the full count. Each carries its `cost_per_month`, its cadence and `cadence_basis`, `uncategorised`, and a `number` with the `action` `cancel`: the person answers that number to cancel it. The numbers follow the last lead and dispute lead, this workspace first, then `other_workspaces` in their order. `candidate_key` names the workspace and the supplier: act on a number only when a fresh measure gives it the same `candidate_key`. Every bank row carries `source`: `both` when the supplier's invoices are merged into it, else `bank`; one supplier is never listed twice. `invoice_candidate_totals` sums every invoice candidate per currency, past the list cap too, and is never added to `totals`. With `partial: true` and no bank in scope, the invoice candidates are still measured: list them as found from received invoices. `invoice_read.status` `side_unknown` or `failed` means the invoices were not read, which is not "no invoice". `invoice_read.rows_truncated: true` means some months missed their smallest suppliers. `invoice_read.category_unread_count` above 0 counts the smallest suppliers whose category was not looked up: an excluded category among them can be listed as uncategorised. `invoice_read.merge_incomplete: true` means the bank labels were not all tied to their invoice suppliers: an invoice line can repeat a bank row paid under a label.

**What pays each one.** Each subscription carries `paid_with`: the means that paid its latest debit (`last_paid_on`). `card_last_four` and `card_name` name the card when Well knows it. `card_connector_slug` names the connector that synced that card, such as `qonto`, and `card_workspace_connector_id` names that connection: a card action runs on it, never on another connection. `account_name` names the account debited. `card_last_four: null` means the debit names no card (a transfer, a direct debit, or a bank that does not say), never "no card". `paid_with: null` means the read named no payer; `payers_truncated: true` means the read hit its cap, so some subscriptions carry none. Show a card as its last four digits only, such as ••1234.

**Never claim a saving.** A possibly ended subscription or a possible duplicate is what the bank shows, and Well cannot see whether a service is in use.

**The yearly leads.** Each subscription carries `rise_per_year`: what its price rise costs over a year, null when the amount did not rise, with `first_cost_per_year` and `latest_cost_per_year`: what it cost a year before the rise and costs a year after it. Quote those two for the old and the new price per year, and never multiply a payment yourself. Each one also carries `rise_per_seat`: that rise for one seat, the rise divided by the stored seat count, to two decimal places. No stored seat count counts as one, so the two figures match. `rise_leads` lists the rises that count as leads: a possibly ended subscription is none, and a copy already counted in `paid_in_several_workspaces` is none, because dropping that copy drops its rise too. `annual_lead_totals` sums, per currency, every rise lead and every extra copy below, with how many it sums. A rise of a supplier known only by its bank label is no lead: `label_only_rises` lists it with the same yearly figures. `bank_rise_count` counts every rise the bank shows, the label-only ones included; a possible duplicate, a dispute lead, a refused payment and an unused tool are never a rise. `yearly_savings` gives, per currency, the yearly saving a reply opens on and each part it sums: `saving_per_year` is `rise_per_year` (every bank rise still paid, label-only ones included, `rise_count` of them) plus `duplicate_per_year` (the extra copies, `duplicate_count` of them). `to_recover` is what the confirmed double charges took twice (`double_charge_count` of them): paid once, never in `saving_per_year`. Quote them as returned: a lead to check, never a saving made.

**Every workspace of the person.** When the person asks where they can save or what they could cut, do not answer from this tool alone: load the `subscription-spend` skill (with well_get_skill, or with the host's own skill tool when the Well skills are installed in it) and follow it, because it orders the answer and names each workspace. A list ask or a rise ask, such as "which subscriptions do I pay?" or "did any of our subscriptions go up?", loads the skill first too, on an AI app host and on WhatsApp; on WhatsApp it takes that same answer across the person's workspaces. On WhatsApp, pass `workspaces: "all_my_workspaces"` on every call. Elsewhere, pass it when the person asks where they can save, what to cut, or about everything they pay across their workspaces. `other_workspaces` returns the measured other-workspace groups selected for named blocks. On WhatsApp, the tool reads up to 10 other workspaces of the login the turn acts as, the starting login or the one picked with `/account`; elsewhere, it reads up to 10 other real workspaces this same signed-in person is a member of. Each returned group comes with its subscriptions, totals and possible duplicates. `workspace_order.workspace_ids` lists at most 10 groups in answer order, including the current workspace when its group holds something. `workspace_groups_omitted` counts measured groups outside that limit; `other_workspaces_omitted` gives each omitted other workspace's descriptor, subscription count and check facts (possible duplicates and possibly ended subscriptions) so the answer can still name them. A group whose read failed, read partially or truncated keeps a named slot ahead of readable groups, so it is never dropped by the cap. `other_workspaces_skipped` counts other workspaces not read; totals and leads use all workspaces measured, including unnamed groups. `paid_in_several_workspaces` holds the suppliers two or more of them pay for what reads as one subscription: the same payee domain, cadence and category, at a comparable cost. When the person may read more workspaces than that, `other_workspaces_skipped` counts the ones not read, and every total covers the workspaces read only. Well finds those workspaces from the person; a workspace is never named in the call, and an AI app connection reaches only the workspaces its grant covers. `all_workspaces_totals` gives, per currency, the subscription count, the cost per month and the cost per year of every workspace read, this one included, and the count and the cost per month of the possibly ended ones among them: each the sum of the workspaces' own `totals`. `other_workspaces_status` says why the list is what it is: `not_requested`, `read`, `no_signed_in_person` or `unreadable` (which is not "no other workspace"). The cards draw this workspace only.

**Workspace names and empty groups.** `leads[].targets`, `kept` and `dispute_leads[].targets` carry each target's `workspace_name`, including a target in a group omitted from `other_workspaces`. `other_workspaces_empty_count` counts other workspaces whose bank was fully read with no subscription and that have no invoice candidate, whatever their invoice read; `other_workspaces_empty_invoices_unread_count` counts those among them whose received invoices were not read.

**The order and the numbers.** `workspace_order.workspace_ids` is the order to list the workspaces in: the biggest cost per year first, in `workspace_order.currency`, and on a tie this workspace (the one the call runs in), else the person's own space. When the call runs in the person's own space, a workspace of a company comes first on a tie. `leads` is every yearly lead `annual_lead_totals` sums, numbered in the order a reply shows them: the biggest `amount_per_year` first, and on a tie the lead acting in this workspace, else in the person's own space, with the same company rule as the workspaces. Each lead carries its `kind` (rise, paid_in_several_workspaces), the one `action` it proposes (renegotiate, cancel_extra_copies) and its `targets`: the workspace and the supplier row each action runs on (a null `workspace_id` is this workspace). A `cancel_extra_copies` lead also names in `kept` the copy it keeps; show the kept copy and the copies cancelled on its line. Show each lead under its `number`, never renumber them: the person answers with these numbers, and the same measure numbers the same leads the same way. `dispute_leads` follow, numbered on from the last lead: one per confirmed pair month of `possible_duplicates` in any workspace read, the biggest `amount_charged_twice` first, each with the `action` contest, its `month` and its one target. `amount_charged_twice` is paid once, so it is never a cost per year and never in `annual_lead_totals`: a dispute lead is still to check, and nothing is contested from here. `lead_key` joins the action, the supplier, the sorted target workspaces, the sorted target supplier rows and the supplier row of the copy kept: when a person answers a number from an earlier answer, act only when the lead under that number in a fresh measure has the same `lead_key` as in the answer they read, because the figures can move and give the number another supplier, action or workspace.

**Naming a workspace.** `workspace` and each `other_workspaces[].workspace` carry `workspace_name`, `own_company_name`, `is_personal` and `bank_names`. Name a workspace from them, by what sets it apart, never by a generic label such as "personal space" alone.

`partial: true` means nothing was measured from the bank: the read was cut short, or the workspace holds no bank account and no credit card. Say so rather than reporting no subscriptions; the invoice candidates are measured apart. `rows_truncated: true` means the smallest counterparties were not read, so every total is a floor.

`scope` is required: `own_and_adopted` is the spend population the burn counts, `own` the workspace's own rows only.

When the person asks about software subscriptions, pass `category: "software"`; it includes software, hosting, AI and sales tools, and excludes rent, insurance and bank fees.

When the token authorizes one workspace, call this directly — no workspace call is needed first. When it authorizes several, this read will not guess which one you mean: pass `workspace_id` on the call.

conversation_id.description: The conversation id returned by the previous Well result, in its meta under well/conversation_id, in its structuredContent, or in its JSON text block. Pass it back on every call in the same conversation, including a call a card makes, so the chosen workspace and the earlier answers still apply. It decides the conversation on its own: nothing the host states about the session replaces it. Omit it only on the first call of a conversation.

scope.description: Which rows are this workspace's: `own_and_adopted` for its spend, `own` for its own rows only. Required; see the description.

workspace_id.description: Target workspace. Omit when the token authorizes one workspace. Required when it authorizes several: this read reports one workspace's own figures and will not choose which.

workspace_scope.description: Restrict this call to the family: the token's primary workspace plus the company workspaces under it that you are a member of. Unrelated authorized workspaces drop out of the read; row reads merge across the family, while a per-workspace figure still reports exactly one workspace.

workspaces.description: Which workspaces the measure reads. Omit it, or pass "this_workspace", for this workspace alone. Pass "all_my_workspaces" on every call on WhatsApp, and elsewhere when the person asks where they can save, what to cut, or what they pay across all their workspaces: `other_workspaces` then measures each other workspace the same signed-in person is a member of.
